checks.after: Later he saw a white hare, galloped to shoot it; his horse fell and he was injured, then he told what he had seen.
checks.reason: Chinese 後見白兔馳射之馬倒被傷乃說所見 requires seeing, gallop-and-shoot, the horse’s fall, and narrating what was seen; “charged…told the omen” omits 見 and invents an omen gloss.

checks.after: He died in the fourth year of Yonghe after fifteen years on the throne, aged fifty-two.
checks.reason: Source gives only 永和四年 with tenure and age; the Western year 348 CE is not in the Chinese sentence and must not be imported.

checks.after: Murong Han.
checks.reason: Unit Chinese is the bare name heading 慕容翰; the parenthetical “defector general” is editorial and not in the source.

checks.after: He was heroic and bold, full of stratagems, ape-armed and skilled at archery, with strength that surpassed others.
checks.reason: 性雄豪多權略猿臂工射膂力過人 needs heroic boldness, stratagems, ape-arms, and surpassing strength; “cunning…superb archer” drops 猿臂 and weakens 權略.

checks.after: When he fled to Duan Liao, he was deeply respected and loved by Liao.
checks.reason: 及奔段遼深為遼所敬愛 states flight to Liao and deep respect-and-love; “honored…after his defection” omits 奔 and flattens 敬愛.

checks.after: After the defeat at Liucheng, Duan Lan wanted to ride the victory and push deep; Murong Han, fearing this would bring harm on his native state, gave Lan deceitful counsel, and Lan then did not advance.
checks.reason: Must keep distinct 乘勝深入、慮成本國之害、詭說于蘭、and 蘭遂不進; the before collapses these into a vague feigned-advice gloss.

checks.after: The King of Yan has come in person; his soldiers and horses are elite.
checks.reason: 燕王自來士馬精銳 requires the Yan king’s personal arrival and elite troops-and-mounts; “Murong Huang’s host is elite” omits 自來 and 士馬.

checks.after: Weapons are ill-omened tools, and battle holds peril; if you lose here, how will you defend the south?”
checks.reason: 兵者凶器戰有危慮若其失利何以南禦乎 must open with the 兵者凶器 idiom; “War is peril” drops that proposition.

checks.after: He then led his forces to pursue Huang, and Lan was indeed crushingly defeated.
checks.reason: 乃率眾追皝蘭果大敗 states leading the host in pursuit and the 果-marked great defeat; “chased…was crushed” omits 率眾 and 果.

checks.after: Although Murong Han dwelt in an enemy state, he established loyalty through the course of events—all cases were of this kind.
checks.reason: 因事立忠皆此類也 is loyalty shown amid events, plus the summarizing 皆此類也; “worked secretly for Yan’s good” invents secrecy and a Yan-benefit gloss.

checks.after: Han then fled, and Gui sent over a hundred picked cavalry to pursue him.
checks.reason: 既而逃歸乃遣勁騎百餘追之 requires Han’s flight before Gui’s pursuit, and 百餘 is over a hundred, not a round hundred alone.

checks.after: You know my bow and arrows well enough—do not press me and bring death on yourselves.
checks.reason: 無為相逼自取死也 warns against pressing him and thereby seeking their own deaths; “do not force a fight” drops 自取死.

checks.after: My bow and arrows you lot fully know; do not press me and seek your own deaths.
checks.reason: 相逼 is pressing the speaker, not forcing each other; 自取死也 is bringing death on yourselves—definite literal errors in the before.

checks.after: Plant a blade at a hundred paces—if I hit it, withdraw;
checks.reason: 吾射中者 means if the shot hits; 刀鐶 appears only in the next unit and must not be imported as “ring it” here.

checks.after: Later, as his illness gradually improved, he tried riding at home to test himself; someone reported that Han was privately practising riding and suspected something extraordinary.
checks.reason: 後疾漸愈騎馬自試或有人告翰私習騎疑為非常 are recovery, self-test, report, and suspicion; “informers called it sedition” omits those steps and over-glosses.

checks.after: Huang, who had long been jealous of him, thereupon granted him death.
checks.reason: 皝素忌之遂賜死焉 is long-standing jealousy/wariness and granting death; poison is only 仰藥而死 later, so “sent him poison” is unsupported here.

checks.after: Huang had long been jealous of him; thereupon granted him death.
checks.reason: 素忌之 needs long-standing jealousy or wariness; “plain envied” misrenders 素 and leaves the jealousy wording unclear.

checks.after: Nearing death Murong Han told the envoy, “Han harbored distrust and fled abroad; my crime is too great for death to atone; I could not leave my bones in a rebel court, so I returned to submit to the authorities.
checks.reason: 翰臨死…罪不容誅…骸骨委賊庭…歸罪有司 are all required; the before drops 臨死, softens 罪不容誅, and misses 賊庭 / 歸罪有司.

checks.after: Han nearing death told the envoy: “Han harbored suspicion and fled abroad; the crime is too great for death to atone; I could not cast my bones in the bandit court; therefore I returned to submit to the responsible officials.
checks.reason: 罪不容誅 is guilt beyond what death can atone, and 歸罪有司 is submitting to the authorities, not “returned guilt to” them.

checks.after: When Wang Jun held the province, Yu was transferred to administration aide; Jun was jealous and would not employ him.
checks.reason: 王浚領州轉治中從事忌而不能任 states the transfer plus jealousy and refusal to employ; “rose…but was distrusted” omits 轉 and flattens 忌而不能任.

checks.after: Shi Le asked, "If what you say is so, why did Duke Wang not employ them?"
checks.reason: Preceding speech names both Liu Han and Yang Yu; 王公何以不任 therefore refers to not employing them, not a singular him.

checks.after: Cheng Pan replied, “Now Huaxia is split and crumbling, the nine provinces torn apart; where proper tracks reach is only as far as the Yi River.
checks.reason: 今華夏分崩九州幅裂軌跡所及易水而已 means civil order’s reach ends at the Yi; “no refuge beyond” and the dropped 九州幅裂 are unfaithful.

checks.after: To wish to live in proud reclusion (as in the “Kao pan”) and wait for a great opening is to wait for the Yellow River to run clear.
checks.reason: 欲偃蹇考槃以待大通者俟河之清也 is one reclusive-waiting proposition with a single 俟河之清 simile; the before doubles the river-clear clause into nonsense.

checks.after: Let both sides remedy their former faults and renew good faith as at the beginning, so the state may have the security of Mount Tai and the common people receive the blessing of laying down their burdens.”
checks.reason: 兩追前失通款如初 is remedy former faults and renew good faith as at first, not “forget old quarrels”; 太山/息肩 images must remain.

checks.after: Murong Huang, who had long heard of Yu’s name, at once ordered his bonds released, appointed him Palace Director, then promoted him to Grand General’s Left Major.
checks.reason: 素聞裕名 is long hearing of the name, not admiration; offices are 郎中令 then 大將軍左司馬, not a vague senior major.

checks.after: Huang had long heard of Yu’s name; immediately ordered his bonds released; appointed Palace Director; promoted him to Grand General’s Left Major.
checks.reason: 素聞 needs “had long heard”; “plain had heard” misrenders 素, while the two office steps stay exact in the replacement.

checks.after: Although Yang Yu served Huang and grew daily closer, with favor and rank above the old retainers, his nature was humble, respectful, pure and frugal, firm, simple, kind and earnest; though he repeatedly held posts at the apex of the court, he was like a scholar in plain cloth.
checks.reason: Must keep 仕皝日近寵秩在舊人之右, the virtue string 謙恭清儉剛簡慈篤, and 曆居朝端若布衣之士; the before heavily compresses them.

checks.after: Earlier, Lu Chen of Fanyang always praised him, saying, “I have lived through Jin’s clear peace and have broadly observed many court gentlemen; loyal, pure, concise and resolute, steadfast in faith and fierce in righteousness—men like Yang Shilun are in truth few.”
checks.reason: Quote needs 初每稱、晉之清平、the full 忠清簡毅篤信義烈 string, and courtesy name 陽士倫; the before thins these into a paraphrase.

checks.after: served the Duan house
checks.reason: 曆事段氏五主 is successively serving the Duan house’s lords, a descriptive service relation, not a post titled “minister of the Duan”.

additionalCorrections.before: You can at a hundred paces set up a blade; if I shoot the center, you then conveniently turn back;
additionalCorrections.after: You can at a hundred paces set up a blade; if my shot hits, you then should turn back;
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 汝可百步豎刀，吾射中者，汝便宜反；
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 吾射中者 uses 中 as the verb “hit,” not a noun “center”; the literal must not read the hit as shooting the center.

additionalCorrections.before: To hide and wait for peace is to wait for the Yellow River to run clear.
additionalCorrections.after: To wish to live in proud reclusion and wait for a great opening is to wait for the Yellow River to run clear.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 欲偃蹇考槃，以待大通者，俟河之清也。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 偃蹇考槃以待大通 is proud reclusion awaiting a great opening, not merely hiding to wait for peace; both English fields needed the fuller propositions.
